subject.title: backup create stalls on large installations (4GB+ .openclaw dir)

question: What restore-safe core behavior should `openclaw backup create` support for large state directories: native smart/custom exclusions, a minimal completion/error fix, or a documented decision that current coarse scopes are the intended core boundary?
rationale: Choosing default exclusions and protected backup contents affects restore completeness and sensitive state handling, so automation should not pick the final policy while a linked PR is already under review.

options.title: Narrow Native Backup Controls
options.body: Use https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/44288 or a replacement as the implementation path after resolving conflicts, proof, protected-path semantics, and upgrade compatibility.

options.title: Ship Minimal Reliability First
options.body: Fix the archive path to complete or fail clearly with progress or size guidance, while deferring smart/custom exclusions to the broader backup-scope tracker.

options.title: Document Core Limits
options.body: Document current core backup limits and point users to plugin or ClawHub alternatives only if maintainers decide native exclusions are outside core for now.

recommendation.title: Narrow Native Backup Controls
recommendation.body: Use https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/44288 or a replacement as the implementation path after resolving conflicts, proof, protected-path semantics, and upgrade compatibility.

likelyOwner.reason: Their backup archive extraction work is the closest code-history signal for routing the restore-safety and backup-scope decision.
